question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The head coach declared that the player who will score the most points in the game will clinch the trophy this year.
option_2: who were score the maximum points
option_3: who have score the maximum points
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. who scores the maximum points.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a sentence with a future main clause and a subordinate clause of condition/time introduced by a relative pronoun, the subordinate clause takes the simple present, not the future. So "who will score" becomes "who scores the maximum points".

◦ Correct: ... the player who scores the maximum points in the game will clinch the trophy this year.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "who scores the points maximum" has wrong word order.

• Option 2 "who were score" and Option 3 "who have score" are grammatically incorrect verb forms.

NOTE

• Rule: In clauses beginning with "who/when/if/until/as soon as", we use the simple present to refer to the future — "The one who comes first will win" (not "will come").

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Despite the challenges, / they ultimate achieved / their goal of launching / their startup.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. they ultimate achieved.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A verb ("achieved") must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. "Ultimate" is an adjective; the correct adverb is "ultimately".

◦ Correct: ... they ultimately achieved their goal of launching their startup.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Despite the challenges,", "their goal of launching" and "their startup" are all correct.

NOTE

• Adjective vs adverb: an adjective describes a noun (the ultimate goal), while an adverb describes a verb (they ultimately achieved). Most adverbs of manner/degree end in "-ly".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word(s) in the given sentence.

Manik said that it is mandatory that each student pay his/her tuition fees every month.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. each student pays.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "each" is always singular and takes a singular verb. In the simple present, a singular subject takes the verb with "-s" → "each student pays".

◦ Correct: ... it is mandatory that each student pays his/her tuition fees every month.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "paids" is not a word.

• Option 3 "paid" is past tense (wrong tense for a general rule).

• Option 4 "each students pay" wrongly makes "student" plural after "each".

NOTE

• "Each / every / one of / either / neither + singular noun + singular verb": "Each boy has a pen", "Every student is present".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Once the seminar was over, the host gave up the certificates to the active participants.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. gave away.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "give away", meaning to distribute or hand out (something), especially prizes/certificates. "Give up" (to quit) is wrong in this context.

◦ Correct: ... the host gave away the certificates to the active participants.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "brought about" (cause to happen), Option 2 "came by" (obtained) and Option 4 "put across" (communicated) do not fit distributing certificates.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "give": give away (distribute/reveal), give up (quit), give in (surrender), give off (emit), give out (distribute / run out).

question:
Rectify the error in the given sentence by selecting the correct spelling from the options provided.

The nights of King Arthur were known for their chivalry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. knights.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The context of "King Arthur" and "chivalry" requires "knights" — medieval mounted warriors of noble rank — not "nights" (periods of darkness). They are homophones. (शूरवीर / योद्धा)

◦ Correct: The knights of King Arthur were known for their chivalry.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Night" (the time of darkness) and "knight" (a warrior) sound alike but differ in spelling and meaning.

• Options 2 "naughts" (zeros) and 3 "knots" (ties in a rope) are unrelated.

NOTE

• King Arthur's "Knights of the Round Table" are legendary. "Chivalry" refers to the medieval knightly code of honour, courage and courtesy.

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

I want to buy the less expensive bike, but with the best mileage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. least.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" and the parallel superlative "the best mileage" indicate that the superlative degree is required — "the least expensive bike" (the cheapest of all).

◦ Correct: I want to buy the least expensive bike, but with the best mileage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "little" and Option 3 "lesser" are not superlatives.

• Option 4 "most less" is grammatically wrong (double form).

NOTE

• Degrees of "little/few (amount)": little – less – least. "The least expensive" = the cheapest. It parallels "the best mileage" (both superlatives with "the").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The teacher asked us to __________ the main idea of the passage in the exam.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. summarise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Summarise" means to give a brief statement of the main points of something. Capturing "the main idea of the passage" is exactly summarising. (सारांश देना)

◦ Correct: The teacher asked us to summarise the main idea of the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "conclusion" is a noun, not a verb (it cannot follow "to").

• Option 3 "underestimate" (to value too low) and Option 4 "plagiarise" (to copy someone's work) do not fit.

NOTE

• "Summarise" (verb) / "summary" (noun). A good summary is brief, covers the main points, and is written in one's own words.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four parts. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error.

The youngest employees / are chosen by the / organisation to / manage the fieldwork.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The youngest employees.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The superlative "youngest" is used to single out one/the highest of a group, but the context here refers generally to a category of employees, so the positive degree "young" is appropriate — "The young employees are chosen ...".

◦ Correct: The young employees are chosen by the organisation to manage the fieldwork.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "are chosen by the", "organisation to" and "manage the fieldwork" are all correct (a proper passive structure).

NOTE

• Use the superlative ("youngest") only when comparing three or more and singling out the extreme one, usually with a defining phrase. For a general description, the positive degree ("young") is correct.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The most effective way to enhance your vocabulary is to look to unknown words in a dictionary.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. look up.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "look up", meaning to search for information (e.g., a word's meaning) in a dictionary or reference book. "Look to" is wrong here.

◦ Correct: ... the most effective way to enhance your vocabulary is to look up unknown words in a dictionary.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "write off" (to cancel/dismiss), Option 3 "set by" (not standard) and Option 4 "stand against" (to oppose) do not fit.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "look": look up (search for information / improve), look after (care for), look for (search), look into (investigate), look up to (admire).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that has a grammatical error.

The thieves had no alternative / but to acquiesce with / the orders of / the police.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. but to acquiesce with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "acquiesce" (to accept or agree reluctantly) takes the preposition "in" or "to", not "with". So it should be "acquiesce in / to the orders".

◦ Correct: The thieves had no alternative but to acquiesce in the orders of the police.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "The thieves had no alternative", "the orders of" and "the police" are all correct.

NOTE

• "Acquiesce" means to agree silently/reluctantly. Correct prepositions: acquiesce in a decision / acquiesce to a demand. Synonyms: comply, consent, submit, yield.

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

The microscopic chip that emits a uniqe signal has been embedded into your arm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. uniqe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Uniqe" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "unique", meaning being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else. (अद्वितीय / अनोखा)

◦ Example: Every fingerprint is unique.

• Spelling key: U + NI + QUE — it ends in "-que" (as in antique, technique, opaque).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Embedded", "emits" and "microscopic" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words ending in "-que" (French origin): unique, antique, technique, boutique, opaque, plaque. The "-que" is pronounced like "k".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Benevolent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Kind.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Benevolent" means well-meaning, kind and generous; wishing to do good to others. Its closest synonym is "kind". (परोपकारी / दयालु)

◦ Example: The benevolent/kind businessman donated to many charities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Enthusiastic" (eager), Option 3 "Mysterious" (puzzling) are unrelated.

• Option 4 "Hostile" (unfriendly) is an antonym of benevolent.

NOTE

• Synonyms of benevolent: kind, kindly, generous, charitable, compassionate, humane.

• Antonyms: malevolent, cruel, unkind, hostile.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Careful
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Cautious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Careful" means taking care to avoid harm or mistakes; attentive and watchful. Its closest synonym is "cautious" (careful to avoid danger). (सतर्क / सावधान)

◦ Example: Be careful/cautious while handling electrical equipment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Corrupt" (dishonest), Option 3 "Captivating" (charming) and Option 4 "Corrosive" (able to corrode) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of careful: cautious, attentive, prudent, watchful, vigilant, meticulous.

• Antonyms: careless, reckless, negligent, hasty.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Poonam used a rubber band to keep the pencils together. 'Band' here means __________.
option_1: a thin ring of rubber used for holding things together
option_2: a long rigid piece of wood or metal
option_4: a range of values or frequencies within a series
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. a thin ring of rubber used for holding things together.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the context "a rubber band to keep the pencils together", the word "band" means "a thin ring/loop (of rubber) used for holding things together". (रबर बैंड / छल्ला)

◦ Example: She tied the papers with a rubber band.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "a long rigid piece of wood or metal" describes a rod/bar, not a band.

• Option 3 "a tube filled with water" is unrelated.

• Option 4 "a range of values or frequencies within a series" is the scientific/technical sense of "band" (e.g., a frequency band), which does not fit this context.

NOTE

• "Band" is a homonym with several meanings: a rubber band (a loop), a music band (a group), a frequency band (a range), a band/strip of colour. Context decides the meaning.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Fulfeel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fulfeel" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Fulfil" (British) / "Fulfill" (American), meaning to carry out or achieve (a task, promise or desire). (पूरा करना)

◦ Example: He worked hard to fulfil his dream of becoming a pilot.

• Spelling key: FUL + FIL — note single "l" in "ful" and the ending "-fil" (British).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Altogether", "Always" and "Until" are all correctly spelt (note each has a single "l": altogether, always, until).

NOTE

• Related forms: fulfil (verb), fulfilment/fulfillment (noun), fulfilling (adjective). Watch the single/double "l": fulfil (UK) / fulfill (US).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word.

The partners ended up being traitorous to each other.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Faithful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Traitorous" means betraying trust; disloyal or treacherous. Its antonym is "faithful", meaning loyal and trustworthy. (विश्वासघाती का विलोम — वफादार)

◦ Example: A traitorous soldier betrayed his country, unlike the faithful ones who defended it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Disloyal" and Option 4 "Fickle" (changeable) are synonyms (or near) of traitorous.

• Option 2 "Proficient" (skilled) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of traitorous: treacherous, disloyal, unfaithful, perfidious.

• Antonyms: faithful, loyal, trustworthy, devoted.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who rules with absolute power and authority
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Dictator.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "dictator" is a ruler with total, absolute power over a country, typically one who has obtained it by force and governs oppressively. (तानाशाह / अधिनायक)

◦ Example: The country suffered under the rule of a cruel dictator.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Senator" — a member of a senate (legislature).

• Option 2 "Ruler" — a general term for one who rules (not necessarily absolute).

• Option 4 "Sovereign" — a supreme ruler/monarch (but not specifically one with oppressive absolute power).

NOTE

• "Dictator" implies absolute and often oppressive power. Related: dictatorship (rule by a dictator), autocrat, despot, tyrant.

question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

The entire audience was all ears when the Indian-born American economist started giving a speech.
option_2: was willing to exit the show
option_3: was arguing in favour of both sides
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. was keen to listen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to be all ears" means to be listening eagerly and attentively; keen to hear what someone has to say. (ध्यान से सुनने को उत्सुक)

◦ Example: Tell me your plan — I'm all ears.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "eager to speak", Option 2 "willing to exit" and Option 3 "arguing in favour of both sides" do not convey attentive listening.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of attention: "lend an ear" (listen), "prick up one's ears" (start listening attentively), "hang on someone's every word".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

He is known for his humility.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Pride.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Humility" means the quality of being humble; a modest view of one's own importance. Its antonym is "pride" (an excessively high opinion of oneself / arrogance). (विनम्रता का विलोम — घमंड)

◦ Example: Despite his success, he showed great humility, without a trace of pride.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Knowledge", Option 3 "Beauty" and Option 4 "Agility" (nimbleness) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of humility: modesty, humbleness, meekness.

• Antonyms: pride, arrogance, conceit, vanity, haughtiness.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Bheem has been shown in the popular culture as someone who eats in large quantity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. eats like a horse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to eat like a horse" means to eat a very large amount of food. It perfectly replaces "eats in large quantity". (बहुत अधिक खाना)

◦ Example: After the workout, he was so hungry that he ate like a horse.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "eat humble pie" — to admit one's mistake humbly.

• Option 3 "eat like a bird" — to eat very little (the opposite).

• Option 4 "chews the fat" — to chat casually.

NOTE

• Contrasting idioms: "eat like a horse" (eat a lot) vs "eat like a bird" (eat very little). Bheem/Bhima from the Mahabharata is famed for his huge appetite.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came _____2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3____ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea _____4_____ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. their.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Their" is the possessive determiner meaning "belonging to them" — the tails belong to the three rats. "a new use for their tails". (उनकी)

◦ Correct: Three big fat rats once found a new use for their tails.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "it's" = "it is" (a contraction, wrong here).

• Option 4 "there" refers to a place.

• Option 1 "the" would be grammatically weaker than the possessive "their".

NOTE

• Confusable words: their (possessive), there (place), they're (they are); its (possessive) vs it's (it is). Here the tails belong to the rats → "their".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came _____2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3____ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea _____4_____ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. creeping.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Creeping" means moving slowly, quietly and carefully (so as not to be noticed). Rats sneaking into a larder at night would be "creeping into" it. (धीरे-धीरे/चुपके से जाना)

◦ Correct: During the night, they came creeping into the larder.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dreaming", Option 2 "acting" and Option 3 "yelling" (shouting) do not suit the stealthy, silent movement of rats at night.

NOTE

• "Creep – crept – crept" means to move slowly and quietly. Synonyms: sneak, tiptoe, slink, steal (in the sense of moving quietly).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came _____2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3____ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea _____4_____ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. narrow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The jar had a "narrow neck" — a small, thin opening — which is why the rats could not reach the treacle with their mouths or paws. This detail explains the problem. (सँकरा / तंग)

◦ Correct: But the jar had a narrow neck ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "funny", Option 3 "obese" (very fat — used for living beings, not a jar's neck) and Option 4 "slow" do not logically describe a jar's neck that blocks access.

NOTE

• "Narrow" = of small width. The narrow neck is the obstacle that makes the rats invent their clever tail-dipping trick. Antonym: wide/broad.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came _____2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3____ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea _____4_____ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. struck.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The collocation "an idea struck someone" means an idea suddenly came to one's mind. So "a bright idea struck one of them". (एक विचार सूझना / मन में आना)

◦ Correct: At last, a bright idea struck one of them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "flew", Option 2 "went" and Option 4 "stood" do not collocate with "idea" in this sense.

NOTE

• Collocations with "idea": an idea struck me / occurred to me / came to me / hit me. "Strike – struck – struck" here means to come suddenly to the mind.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came _____2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3____ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea _____4_____ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. off.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "lick off" means to remove (something) by licking. The rats licked the treacle off the tail. (चाटकर हटाना / उतारना)

◦ Correct: ... allowed the two rats to lick it off.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "lick at" (to lick tentatively), "lick by" and "lick in" do not convey removing the treacle from the tail.

NOTE

• Phrasal verb "lick off" = to remove by licking. Similar: wipe off, brush off, wash off, rub off (all meaning to remove something from a surface).

question:
According to Labour and Employment Statistics 2022, match the states in the first column with their rate of unemployment in the year 2020-21 given in the second column.

i) Kerala   ii) Goa   iii) Haryana   iv) Uttarakhand   |   a) 6.3%   b) 10.1%   c) 6.9%   d) 10.5%
option_1: i) a, ii) c, iii) d, iv) b
option_2: i) d, ii) b, iii) c, iv) a
option_3: i) d, ii) c, iii) b, iv) a
option_4: i) b, ii) d, iii) a, iv) c
solution_text:
The correct answer is i) b, ii) d, iii) a, iv) c.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Labour and Employment Statistics 2022 (unemployment rate, 2020-21), the correct matching is:

◦ i) Kerala → b) 10.1%

◦ ii) Goa → d) 10.5%

◦ iii) Haryana → a) 6.3%

◦ iv) Uttarakhand → c) 6.9%

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4 (i-b, ii-d, iii-a, iv-c).

Additional Information

• The unemployment rate is the percentage of persons unemployed among the total labour force.

• Employment/unemployment data in India is collected through the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by the National Statistical Office (NSO).

NOTE

• Key labour indicators: Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR).

question: Which of the following dance forms is primarily associated with Eastern India states like Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhau.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chhau" is a semi-classical dance form primarily associated with the Eastern Indian states of Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal. It is a martial, tribal and folk dance form. (छऊ नृत्य — पूर्वी भारत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chhau has three main styles: Seraikela Chhau (Jharkhand), Purulia Chhau (West Bengal) and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).

• Chhau was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

• The Seraikela and Purulia styles use masks, while the Mayurbhanj style does not.

NOTE

• Chhau draws themes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and local folklore, and is often performed during the Chaitra Parva festival.

question: Which Articles of the Constitution of India provide for a parliamentary form of government at the Centre?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Articles 74 and 75.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Articles 74 and 75 provide for the parliamentary form of government at the Centre:

◦ Article 74 — provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President.

◦ Article 75 — deals with the appointment, tenure and responsibility of the Council of Ministers (collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• At the State level, the corresponding provisions are Articles 163 and 164 (Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister).

• India follows the Westminster (British) model of parliamentary democracy.

NOTE

• Key features of parliamentary government: nominal (President) and real (PM) executives, collective responsibility, majority rule, and dissolution of the Lower House.

question: Which of the following crops is grown in the Kharif season in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Soyabean.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Soyabean (Soybean)" is a Kharif crop in India — sown with the onset of the southwest monsoon (June–July) and harvested in September–October. (सोयाबीन — खरीफ फसल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kharif crops (monsoon crops): rice, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, groundnut, soybean, tur (arhar).

• Rabi crops (winter crops): wheat, barley, gram, mustard, peas (sown Oct–Dec, harvested Mar–Apr). So mustard and barley are Rabi crops.

• Zaid crops (summer): cucumber, watermelon, muskmelon, bitter gourd.

NOTE

• "Kharif" comes from the Arabic word for "autumn"; these crops need high temperature and humidity and depend on the monsoon rains.

question: What was the percentage increase in the disbursal of 'Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana' (PMMY) loans in the first quarter of FY 2023-24 compared to the same quarter in the previous year, if the disbursal reached ₹81,597 crore, up from ₹62,650 crore?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 23%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The disbursal of PMMY loans rose from about ₹62,650 crore to ₹81,597 crore, an increase of about ₹18,947 crore, which is approximately a 23% increase as per the reported figures. (पीएम मुद्रा योजना — लगभग 23% वृद्धि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY), launched in 2015, provides collateral-free loans up to ₹10 lakh (later enhanced) to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises through MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency).

• Loan categories: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (₹50,000–₹5 lakh), Tarun (₹5–10 lakh).

NOTE

• MUDRA aims to "fund the unfunded" and promote self-employment and entrepreneurship, especially among women, SCs, STs and OBCs.

question: In which of the following years was the 'Quit India Movement' launched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1942.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Quit India Movement" (also called the August Kranti / August Movement) was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942 at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee, demanding an end to British rule. (भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन — 1942)

• Gandhi gave the famous slogan "Do or Die".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The movement began after the failure of the Cripps Mission (1942).

• Most Congress leaders were arrested; the movement saw widespread mass participation, and parallel governments were set up in places like Satara, Ballia and Tamluk.

NOTE

• Other key years: Non-Cooperation Movement (1920), Civil Disobedience/Dandi March (1930), Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919).

question: A person having stunted growth and discoloured hair is most probably suffering from __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Protein Deficiency.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A person (especially a child) with stunted growth and discoloured hair is most probably suffering from protein deficiency. Severe protein deficiency causes diseases like Kwashiorkor (marked by stunted growth, swelling and hair discolouration) and Marasmus. (प्रोटीन की कमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Proteins are the "building blocks of the body", essential for growth, repair and enzymes/hormones.

• Kwashiorkor results from a diet low in protein but adequate in calories; Marasmus results from a deficiency of both protein and calories.

NOTE

• Rich sources of protein: pulses, milk, eggs, meat, fish, soybean and nuts. This is a nutrition topic frequently asked in SSC.

question: In the case of reptiles, their heart is not properly divided in to four chambers i.e., it consists of two auricles and an incompletely divided ventricle. Which of the following is an example of a reptile having a four-chambered heart?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Crocodile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Although most reptiles have a three-chambered heart (two auricles and one incompletely divided ventricle), the crocodile is a special exception — it has a completely divided, four-chambered heart (two auricles and two ventricles). (मगरमच्छ — चार-कक्षीय हृदय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Snakes, turtles and lizards have the usual three-chambered reptilian heart.

• A four-chambered heart allows better separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

NOTE

• Heart chambers: Fishes – 2; Amphibians & most Reptiles – 3; Crocodiles, Birds & Mammals – 4.

question: Samrat Choudhary and Vijay Kumar Sinha became the Deputy Chief Minister of __________ on 28 January 2024.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Samrat Choudhary and Vijay Kumar Sinha were sworn in as the Deputy Chief Ministers of Bihar on 28 January 2024, when Nitish Kumar formed a new government. (बिहार के उप-मुख्यमंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bihar's capital is Patna; it is one of the most populous states of India.

• The office of Deputy Chief Minister is not mentioned in the Constitution but is a common political practice in coalition governments.

NOTE

• A Deputy CM holds the rank of a Cabinet Minister; the post is created for political/administrative convenience.

question: Which of the following is the autobiography of Bhishma Sahni?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aaj ke Ateet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aaj ke Ateet" (Today's Pasts) is the autobiography of the famous Hindi writer Bhishma Sahni. (भीष्म साहनी की आत्मकथा — 'आज के अतीत')

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bhishma Sahni is best known for his novel "Tamas", which depicts the horrors of the Partition of India (1947); it was later made into a television series.

• He received the Padma Bhushan and the Sahitya Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Bhishma Sahni was the younger brother of the actor Balraj Sahni. "Tamas" won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1975.

question: In which year was the Multi-dimensional Poverty Index launched in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2021.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's first National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) was launched by NITI Aayog in 2021. (राष्ट्रीय बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक — 2021)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The National MPI measures poverty across three dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — through 12 indicators, based on the global methodology of the OPHI (Oxford) and UNDP.

• Bihar, Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh had the highest multidimensional poverty.

NOTE

• A person is "multidimensionally poor" if deprived in at least one-third (weighted) of the indicators. This index complements the traditional income-based poverty measure.

question: Valabhi type of Nagara temples are generally __________ in shape, with a roof that rises into a vaulted chamber.
solution_text:
The correct answer is rectangular.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Valabhi" type of Nagara temple is generally rectangular in shape, with a roof that rises into a vaulted (wagon-vaulted) chamber, resembling the shape of a bamboo/wooden barrel-vaulted hut. (वलभी शैली — आयताकार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Nagara (North Indian) style has several sub-types based on the shape of the shikhara: Latina/Rekha-Prasada (curvilinear, square base), Phamsana (broader, shorter, sloping roof) and Valabhi (rectangular, vaulted roof).

NOTE

• The three main temple architectural styles in India are Nagara (North), Dravida (South) and Vesara (Deccan, hybrid).

question: Who among the following founded the Saluva dynasty of Vijayanagara empire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narsimha Deva Raya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Saluva dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire was founded by Saluva Narasimha Deva Raya in 1485, replacing the first (Sangama) dynasty. (सालुव वंश — नरसिंह देव राय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The four dynasties that ruled Vijayanagara were: Sangama → Saluva → Tuluva → Aravidu.

• Krishnadeva Raya (the greatest Vijayanagara ruler) belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.

• Bukka Raya I and Harihara I (the Sangama brothers) founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336.

NOTE

• The Vijayanagara capital Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The empire was weakened after the Battle of Talikota (1565).

question: Who was the chairman of the drafting committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhimrao Ambedkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. B. R. (Bhimrao) Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India, which prepared the draft of the Indian Constitution. He is therefore called the "Father / Chief Architect of the Indian Constitution". (डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर — प्रारूप समिति अध्यक्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947 and had seven members.

• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly; Sir B. N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor.

NOTE

• The Constituent Assembly took about 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to frame the Constitution, which was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

question: The Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur iron ore belt lies in which of the following groups of states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh - Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur iron ore belt lies in the states of Chhattisgarh (Durg, Bastar) and Maharashtra (Chandrapur). It contains very high-grade hematite iron ore. (दुर्ग-बस्तर-चंद्रपुर पेटी — छत्तीसगढ़-महाराष्ट्र)

• The famous Bailadila range in Bastar has some of the best iron ore in the world, exported to Japan via Visakhapatnam port.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other major iron ore belts of India: Orissa-Jharkhand belt (Mayurbhanj, Singhbhum), Bellary-Chitradurga-Ballari-Tumkur belt (Karnataka) and Maharashtra-Goa belt.

NOTE

• India is one of the largest producers of iron ore. Types of iron ore (by iron content, high to low): Magnetite > Hematite > Limonite > Siderite.

question: Which team won the Ultimate Kho-Kho League Season 2 event?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat Giants.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gujarat Giants won the Ultimate Kho-Kho League Season 2 title. (अल्टीमेट खो-खो लीग सीज़न 2 — गुजरात जायंट्स)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The inaugural (Season 1) Ultimate Kho-Kho League (2022) was won by the Odisha Juggernauts.

• Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian tag/pursuit sport; the league is a franchise-based professional competition to popularise it.

NOTE

• India hosted the first Kho-Kho World Cup (2025) in New Delhi, with the Indian men's and women's teams winning the titles.

question: Which of the following was the first Regional Rural Bank of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pratham Bank.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Prathama Bank (Pratham Bank)" was the first Regional Rural Bank (RRB) of India, established on 2 October 1975 in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, sponsored by the Syndicate Bank. (प्रथमा बैंक — पहला क्षेत्रीय ग्रामीण बैंक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were set up on the recommendation of the Narasimham Working Group under the RRB Act, 1976, to provide credit and banking facilities in rural areas.

• Each RRB is jointly owned by the Central Government (50%), the State Government (15%) and a Sponsor Bank (35%).

NOTE

• The first RRBs were established following the Banking Commission's recommendations to serve small farmers, artisans and rural entrepreneurs.

question: The elements that are liquid at room temperature (25°C) are:
solution_text:
The correct answer is bromine and mercury.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the elements, only two are liquid at room temperature (25°C) — a non-metal, bromine (Br), and a metal, mercury (Hg). (कक्ष ताप पर द्रव — ब्रोमीन एवं पारा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chlorine and helium are gases at room temperature, so options containing them are wrong.

• Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature (used in thermometers/barometers).

• A few other elements (like caesium, gallium, rubium) melt just slightly above room temperature.

NOTE

• Elements are classified by state at room temperature into solids (most), liquids (only bromine and mercury) and gases (H, N, O, F, Cl, and the noble gases).

question: Article __________ supplements the 11th fundamental duty of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 21.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 11th Fundamental Duty [Article 51A(k)] asks a parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child (aged 6–14 years). This is supplemented by Article 21A (Right to Education), which makes free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 a Fundamental Right. (अनुच्छेद 21A — शिक्षा का अधिकार)

• Both the 11th duty and Article 21A were added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3 (Article 21 / 21A).

Additional Information

• Article 21 guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty; Article 21A (added in 2002) provides the Right to Education.

• Article 45 (a Directive Principle) was also amended to focus on early childhood care and education below 6 years.

NOTE

• The 11th Fundamental Duty, Article 21A, and the amendment of Article 45 together form the "education package" of the 86th Amendment (2002).

question: Maitraka dynasty was founded in which part of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Western.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Maitraka dynasty was founded in Western India, with its capital at Vallabhi in the Saurashtra region of present-day Gujarat. (मैत्रक वंश — पश्चिमी भारत, वल्लभी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Maitrakas ruled roughly from the 5th to 8th centuries CE, after the decline of the Gupta Empire.

• Vallabhi was a famous centre of learning and Buddhism, with a renowned university, visited by the Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang.

NOTE

• Vallabhi's university is often compared with Nalanda as a great centre of ancient Indian learning. The "Valabhi" temple style is also named after this region.

question: Sonu Nigam was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for which of the following fields?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Art.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous playback singer Sonu Nigam was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 in the field of "Art" (music). (सोनू निगम — पद्म श्री 2022, कला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Padma Awards (Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri) are among the highest civilian honours of India, announced on the eve of Republic Day.

• They are given in various fields such as Art, Social Work, Public Affairs, Science and Engineering, Trade and Industry, Medicine, Literature and Education, Civil Service and Sports.

NOTE

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award (after Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan).

question: For transporting water from one place to another, some man-made structures used to distribute water to a place far away are known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is aqueducts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aqueducts" are man-made structures (channels, bridges or conduits) built to carry and distribute water from one place to another, often over long distances. (जलसेतु / एक्वेडक्ट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• An "aquifer" is a natural underground layer of rock/soil that holds and yields groundwater (not man-made).

• An "aquiclude" is a rock layer that holds water but does not transmit it easily; an "aquifuge" neither holds nor transmits water.

NOTE

• Ancient civilisations (especially the Romans) were famous for building grand aqueducts to supply water to their cities. Aqueducts are also part of modern canal/irrigation systems.

question: Which of the following awards is NOT sponsored by the Madhya Pradesh government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tagore Ratna.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given awards, "Tagore Ratna" is NOT sponsored by the Madhya Pradesh government. The Devi Ahilyabai Award, Kishore Kumar Samman and Tulsi Samman are all instituted by the Madhya Pradesh government. (तानसेन/तुलसी/किशोर कुमार सम्मान — मध्य प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Some awards of the Madhya Pradesh government: Tansen Samman (Hindustani music), Kalidas Samman (classical arts), Kishore Kumar Samman (cinema), Tulsi Samman (folk/tribal art), Iqbal Samman and Maithili Sharan Gupt Samman.

NOTE

• "Tagore Award for Cultural Harmony" is a national award instituted by the Government of India (Ministry of Culture) in 2012 — not by Madhya Pradesh.

question: Who among the following was the chief guest of India's first Republic Day in 1950?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sukarno.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The chief guest at India's first Republic Day (26 January 1950) was President Sukarno of Indonesia (Indonesia's first President). (पहला गणतंत्र दिवस — सुकर्णो, इंडोनेशिया)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India celebrates Republic Day on 26 January to mark the coming into force of the Constitution of India in 1950.

• Inviting a foreign Head of State/Government as the chief guest at the Republic Day parade is a long-standing diplomatic tradition.

NOTE

• 26 January was chosen because the "Purna Swaraj" (complete independence) declaration was first celebrated on that date in 1930 (Lahore Session).

question: Who among the following was the first Indian representative in modern Olympics?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Norman Pritchard.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Norman Pritchard was the first Indian representative in the modern Olympics. He competed at the 1900 Paris Olympics and won two silver medals (in the 200 m sprint and 200 m hurdles), becoming India's first Olympic medallist. (नॉर्मन प्रिचर्ड — पहला ओलंपिक प्रतिनिधि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• KD Jadhav was the first individual Indian to win an Olympic medal after independence (bronze in wrestling, 1952 Helsinki).

• Nilima Ghosh was one of the first Indian women athletes to compete at the Olympics (1952).

NOTE

• The modern Olympic Games were revived in 1896 (Athens) by Pierre de Coubertin. India first participated as a nation (with a team) in 1920 (Antwerp).
